name: breadcrumb-siblings
title: Breadcrumb with siblings
description: A breadcrumb where each level opens a menu of its siblings, so people move sideways without going up first. Long trails fold, long lists filter.
docs: items is the trail from the top to the page you are on: { label, href, siblings }. The last item is the current page and is not a link. A crumb with siblings, a list of { label, href } for the pages at its level (itself included), gets a small chevron beside its label: the label stays a link to the crumb's own page and the chevron is a separate button named 'Pages in Projects' ('Pages in {label}'), so both actions work from the keyboard. The menu checks the entry whose href is the crumb's own (aria-current is 'location' for a level above and 'page' for the last crumb), and a list of twelve or fewer opens as a menu. A longer list opens as a dialog instead, named 'Pages in Projects', because a menu may hold only items and not a field: the filter field is in focus, typing filters, Enter follows the first match, Arrow Down moves into the links and Arrow Up from the first one returns to the field, Escape closes, the number of matches is said politely ('5 of 18 pages') and a filter that matches nothing says so. onNavigate(href) takes a plain click on a crumb or a sibling, for a client router; without it the links are followed, and a modified click always opens the address. maxVisible (default 4) is the most crumbs shown: a longer trail keeps the first crumb and the last maxVisible minus one, and the levels in between fold into a menu behind a '...' button right after the first crumb (named 'Show 2 more levels', or 'Show 1 more level'). separator is a slash by default and can be any node. It is built on Breadcrumb, so the nav landmark, the ordered list, the hidden separators and aria-current are the same as the plain one; labels holds the words for another language. The trail stays on one line and measures itself: when it does not fit its box, more levels fold into the same menu, one at a time starting next to the first crumb, until the label of the current page is whole (the first crumb and the current page always stay), and they come back when the box grows. Short of that only the label of the current page gives way, with an ellipsis; the other crumbs keep their labels, up to a maximum width, and the gaps tighten on a phone.
